target_customer: Developers and startups using coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) who want repeatable, checked workflows
problem: Coding agents patch single cases, drop instructions or write brittle checks. Method turns a repeated task into a workflow with checks and run records so the agent can improve it.
business_model: Freemium developer tool: free plan, 500 USD per month Startup plan, open source CLI

founders.name: Theodore (Teddy) Li
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page for Zenobia Pay; not shown as part of the current Method team of one.

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow runner and run logging layered on existing coding agents via a CLI. Moderate engineering, little original research.

defensibility.rationale: Agent vendors and open source tools can add workflow checks quickly, and the product depends on third party agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Agent vendors keep adding skills and workflow features, but no specific copy of Method was found.

market_need_then: Coding agent use exploded in 2025. The company argues agents fail at consistent repeated work. No customer evidence found.

identity.visual_style: Plain developer product page with a worked radiology report example
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and technical, tagline Agents that improve

brand_strength.rationale: Very generic name and no press or community evidence found.

pivots.from: Zenobia Pay, pay by bank payments for luxury brands (YC launch dated 2026-02-11 by Fondo)
pivots.why: Not stated. The YC page lists Zenobia Pay as a launch under the Method listing, so the order and timing of the two products is unclear.

outcome_analysis: Method is listed as active with a team of one and no verified funding. The YC listing combines Method with an earlier or parallel product, Zenobia Pay, and the current site sells an agent workflow tool. With no revenue, customers or round found, and an unclear pivot, no outcome judgment can be made beyond the high copy risk from agent vendors.
notes: VCBacked lists 500K pre-seed (June 2025, YC) for Zenobia Pay and Dealroom lists a 500 to 750K enterprise value; both aggregators, unverified, not recorded as rounds. A Feedbagel summary claiming Zenobia Pay struggled with adoption conflicts with other sources and is ignored. No competitor sourced near the Spring 2025 batch for either product; Trustly and Volt pay by bank items are undated or later. Founder education and employers not found.
